newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLL-Guilder rise seen staving off Dutch rate hike.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Guilder rise seen staving off Dutch rate hike.

text.p: The Dutch central bank is not expected to raise its money market intervention rate, the special advances rate, on Thursday, according to a Reuters poll.

A poll of 10 bank economists found that none of them expected the central bank to change the special advances rate, which sets the tone for money market rates, when it sets a new pact for lending to commercial banks at 1400 GMT.
Speculation about a rate hike increased earlier this week when the guilder weakened against the mark to below its central parity rate under the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
The central parity rate is 1.12673 guilders to the mark.

Economists said the guilder had since strengthened against the mark, alleviating the need for the central bank to raise rates to prop up the Dutch currency. But some added that the bank would base its decision on the exchange rate at 1400 GMT.
The mark was trading at 1.1263 guilders at 0930 GMT, compared with a near four-year high of 1.1269 on Tuesday.

"They will wait until the last moment to decide whether or not to hike the rate -- and looking at the guilder/mark rate now -- they will leave it unchanged," said economist Michel van der Stee of Van Lanschot Bankiers.

The special advances rate was last raised on July 10, when it was increased by 10 basis points to 3.00 percent, the same level as its German equivalent, the repo rate. The central bank said at the time the move was prompted by guilder weakness.
POLL CONTRIBUTORS: ING, ABN AMRO, MeesPierson, Rabobank, Generale Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Effectenbank Stroeve, Van Lanschot Bankiers, NIB Securities and IRIS.
